system.title: Legal System
system.content: Mixed: Civil law and common law - Constitution of 1972 revised
system.details: Cameroon has a mixed legal system, influenced by both French civil law and English common law. The Constitution of 1972, revised several times, constitutes the fundamental law.

codes.title: Important Codes
codes.content: Civil Code, Penal Code, OHADA, Investment Code
codes.details: The main legal codes include the Civil Code, the Penal Code, the uniform acts of OHADA, and the Investment Code which governs economic activities.

jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions
jurisdictions.content: Supreme Court, Courts of Appeal, Courts of First Instance
jurisdictions.details: The judicial system includes the Supreme Court (highest jurisdiction), the Courts of Appeal, and the Courts of First Instance distributed throughout the territory.

hero.title: Legal and Fiscal Framework
hero.subtitle: Understanding the legal and fiscal context for successful investments in Cameroon.

introduction.title: Presentation of the Legal and Fiscal Framework in Cameroon
introduction.text: Cameroon, a Central African country, has a legal and fiscal framework designed to promote investments and regulate economic activities. It is a hybrid system, blending modernity and tradition, with laws adapted to the needs of local and international economic players.

legalFramework.title: Legal Framework
legalFramework.text: Cameroon has a legal system based on civil law and customary law, while integrating specificities related to its regional and historical context. The main laws include the Investment Code, the Labour Code, and the Commercial Code.

civilLaw.title: Civil Law
civilLaw.text: Inherited from the French tradition, civil law is the main foundation of the Cameroonian legal system. It is based on written texts, such as codes and laws adopted by the government.

customaryLaw.title: Customary Law
customaryLaw.text: Inspired by local traditions and customs, it coexists with civil law and is mainly used in family, inheritance, and land matters, particularly in rural communities.

investmentCode.title: The Investment Code
investmentCode.text: This code establishes the rules and incentives to encourage national and foreign investments. It offers tax advantages, customs exemptions, and a stable environment for investors.

laborCode.title: The Labour Code
laborCode.text: This text governs the relations between employers and employees. It sets the rights and obligations of both parties, such as employment conditions, remuneration, workplace safety, and conflict resolution.

commercialCode.title: The Commercial Code
commercialCode.text: It regulates commercial and industrial activities. It covers areas such as commercial contracts, companies, bankruptcy, and the settlement of commercial disputes.

landRegulation.title: Land Regulation
landRegulation.text: The land legal framework is crucial for investors wishing to acquire land. It differentiates between land belonging to the private, public, or customary domain.

firstInstanceCourts.title: Courts of First Instance
firstInstanceCourts.text: For ordinary civil, criminal, and commercial cases.

supremeCourt.title: The Supreme Court
supremeCourt.text: The highest court in the country.

administrativeTribunals.title: Administrative Tribunals
administrativeTribunals.text: For disputes involving the public administration.

legalFramework.conclusion: The country is also a member of the Organization for the Harmonization of Business Law in Africa (OHADA), which ensures the application of harmonized business law in 17 African countries.

fiscalFramework.title: Fiscal Framework
fiscalFramework.text: Cameroon has put in place a structured tax system, designed to collect the resources necessary for economic development while encouraging investments.

corporateTax.title: Corporate Income Tax (CIT)
corporateTax.text: Standard rate: 30% on profits - Foreign companies may be subject to a 15% withholding tax on their income in Cameroon.

incomeTax.title: Personal Income Tax (PIT)
incomeTax.text: Progressive, with rates ranging from 11% to 38%, depending on the income level.

vat.title: Value Added Tax (VAT)
vat.text: Standard rate: 19.25% - Possible exemptions for certain goods and services, particularly those related to priority sectors such as agriculture and education.

customsDuties.title: Customs Duties
customsDuties.text: Customs duties vary depending on the imported products, with preferential rates for imports from certain countries or regional blocs such as CEMAC (Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa).

otherTaxes.title: Other Taxes
otherTaxes.text: Tax on Economic Activities (TAE), Property Tax, Excise Duties on certain products (alcohol, tobacco, fuel).

investmentCode.title: The Investment Code
investmentCode.text: Temporary exemptions from corporate income tax for new companies.

bilateralAgreements.title: Bilateral Agreements
bilateralAgreements.text: Reduction of customs duties for the import of industrial equipment.

sectoralIncentives.title: Sectoral Incentives
sectoralIncentives.text: VAT exemptions for certain priority sectors such as agriculture or renewable energies.

fiscalFramework.conclusion: The tax administration is supervised by the Directorate General of Taxes (DGI), which ensures the collection of revenue and the application of tax laws. Dematerialization measures have been implemented to facilitate tax declarations and reduce administrative delays.

opportunities.title: Opportunities
opportunities.text: Cameroon offers numerous investment opportunities in various sectors, such as agriculture, energy, infrastructure, new technologies, etc.

regionalHarmonization.title: Regional Harmonization
regionalHarmonization.text: Membership in OHADA and CEMAC guarantees legal and fiscal uniformity with other countries in the region, which facilitates trade.

fiscalIncentives.title: Fiscal Incentives
fiscalIncentives.text: The numerous advantages provided by the Investment Code make Cameroon an attractive destination for investors.

legalStability.title: Legal Stability
legalStability.text: A structured and constantly improving legal framework.

cadre_juridique_fiscal.conclusionFinal: Cameroon has a robust legal and fiscal framework that combines modernity and tradition. Its laws and institutions aim to create a favorable environment for investment and economic development, while ensuring a certain stability. However, efforts are still needed to simplify administrative procedures, strengthen transparency, and further promote the country's attractiveness.

hero.title: Discover Cameroon
hero.subtitle: A country of opportunities and diversity

welcome.title2: The Ideal Destination for Your Investments
welcome.p1: Cameroon, the true economic locomotive of Central Africa, is distinguished by a diversified and resilient economy, offering a favorable environment for investment. With a nominal GDP estimated at USD 45 billion and a sustained economic growth rate of between 4 and 5% per year, the country is positioning itself as a strategic hub for business in Africa.
welcome.h4: A Diversified Economy with Dynamic Sectors
welcome.li1: Cameroon is a world leader in the production of cocoa and coffee, in addition to a varied offer including bananas, cotton, palm oil and tea.
welcome.li2: A strong industrial base driven by food processing, textiles, wood, cement and petroleum products.
welcome.li3: Booming sectors such as telecommunications, finance, transport and tourism, supported by growing demand.
welcome.p2: Cameroon also benefits from a strategic geographical position, connecting Central and West Africa to a potential market of more than 200 million consumers via CEMAC.
welcome.p3: With a young and dynamic workforce, abundant natural resources and a liberal economy open to foreign investors, Cameroon offers unique opportunities in key sectors such as agriculture, energy, infrastructure and new technologies.

priorities.title: Government Priorities
priorities.p1: Cameroon's long-term vision as an emerging, democratic and united country by 2035 has led to a global reflection and the adoption of the orientations contained in the Growth and Employment Strategy Paper (GESP). The GESP, as a reference guidance document valid for a ten-year period (2010-2020), identifies the objectives that Cameroon has set for itself during this period, which can be summarized as follows:
priorities.li1: raise growth to an average level of 5.5% per year by 2020;
priorities.li3: reduce the poverty rate to around 28% in 2020.
priorities.p2: To achieve these 3 main objectives, three strategies have been defined, namely:

installation.desc: During the first years, the State supports you with total exemptions to ease your start-up and reduce your initial financial risk.

exploitation.title: Operation Phase

cta.subtitle: These tax incentives, combined with a one-stop shop and a skilled workforce, make Cameroon the destination of choice for your growth.

cta.title: Secure your investment
cta.subtitle: These rights and guarantees provide you with a solid legal framework to develop your project in Cameroon with peace of mind and confidence.

protection.title: Investment Protection
protection.description: Cameroon provides robust investment protection through its **2013 Investment Code**, international conventions and membership of **OHADA**.
protection.dialogIntro: Cameroon has established a solid legal framework to guarantee the security of investments, both domestic and foreign.

blocks.b1_i1: **Investment Code (Law No. 2013/004)**: freedom of investment, property rights and non-expropriation without compensation.
blocks.b1_i2: **OHADA Law**: unified and modern business law securing all commercial transactions.
blocks.b1_i3: **CIPRES and CIMA Conventions**: stable framework for risk management and insurance.
blocks.b2_i1: **Protection against expropriation**: only for public interest purposes and subject to fair compensation.
blocks.b2_i2: **Tax stability**: exemption periods of up to 10 years for certain priority sectors.
blocks.b2_i3: **Freedom of capital transfer**: free repatriation of profits, dividends and liquidation proceeds.
blocks.b2_i4: **Non-discriminatory treatment**: equality between domestic and foreign investors (National Treatment + MFN Clause).

traitement.title: National Treatment and MFN Clause
traitement.description: Investors benefit from the **same treatment** as nationals and advantages granted to other countries (**MFN clause**).
traitement.dialogIntro: Cameroonian legislation guarantees fair and non-discriminatory treatment to foreign investors.

blocks.b1_i1: Foreign investors enjoy the **same rights and obligations** as domestic investors.
blocks.b1_i2: Applicable at all stages: establishment, operation, acquisition of assets and public procurement.
blocks.b1_i3: Objective: **eliminate all discrimination** based on nationality or origin of capital.
blocks.b2_i1: Any advantage granted to another country is **automatically extended** to investors covered by the MFN clause.
blocks.b2_i2: Guarantees equal treatment among all international partners.
blocks.b3_i1: Certain **strategic sectors** (defence, critical natural resources) may have specific regimes.
blocks.b3_i2: **Safeguard measures** may be applied in exceptional situations.

resources.r2: Learn more about the MFN clause (WTO)

cadre_legal.title: Legal Framework and Institutions
cadre_legal.description: Cameroon has a **modern legal framework** and dedicated institutions to support investors.
cadre_legal.dialogIntro: Cameroon relies on a robust legislative and institutional framework to regulate and support investments.

blocks.b1_i1: **API** (Investment Promotion Agency): one-stop shop, support and facilitation of procedures.
blocks.b1_i2: **MINEPAT**: responsible for economic policy and supervision of major projects.
blocks.b1_i3: **Business Formalities Centres (CFE)**: simplify company creation by grouping all administrations.
blocks.b1_i4: **OHADA ORD**: internationally recognised arbitration and mediation mechanisms.
blocks.b2_i1: **OHADA Law**: 10 Uniform Acts covering all areas of business law.
blocks.b2_i2: **Investment Code (Law No. 2013/004)**: principles, incentive schemes and guarantees.
blocks.b2_i3: **General Tax Code**: corporate and personal income taxation.
blocks.b2_i4: **Labour Code**: employer-employee relations, employment and dismissal conditions.
blocks.b2_i5: **Public Procurement Code**: transparency and competition in public contracts.

droit_propriete.title: Right to Property
droit_propriete.description: **Private property is guaranteed** by the Constitution, with clear land tenure systems to secure your acquisitions.
droit_propriete.dialogIntro: The right to property is fundamental and firmly embedded in Cameroonian legislation.

blocks.b1_i1: **Land Title**: irrefutable proof of ownership, issued by MINDCAF. Valid for 25 renewable years.
blocks.b1_i2: **Long-term Lease (Bail Emphytéotique)**: long duration (18 to 99 years) with real rights on the land, usable as bank collateral.
blocks.b1_i3: **Property Certificate**: provisional document attesting to a pending application.
blocks.b1_i4: **State Land**: the State is the initial owner; acquisition via concessions convertible into land titles.
blocks.b2_i1: **Cadastral Registration**: mandatory with physical boundary marking and topographic survey.
blocks.b2_i2: **Publication in the Official Gazette**: ensures transparency for third parties.
blocks.b2_i3: **Non-Retrocession Certificate**: guarantees the land has not been returned.
blocks.b2_i4: **Land Register Consultation**: verify history before any acquisition.

procedure_terrain.title: Land Acquisition Procedures
procedure_terrain.description: **Simplified procedures** facilitate land acquisition for investment projects, with known timelines.
procedure_terrain.dialogIntro: Land acquisition is governed by clear procedures designed to facilitate the steps for investors.

blocks.b1_i1: **Application Submission**: to MINDCAF or API, with detailed project description.
blocks.b1_i2: **Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)**: mandatory for large-scale projects.
blocks.b1_i3: **Land Use Plan Approval**: compliance with urban planning and local regulations.
blocks.b1_i4: **Payment of Land Rights**: registration fees, land taxes and applicable royalties.
blocks.b1_i5: **Issuance of Land Title**: definitive title or signed concession contract.
blocks.b2_i1: **Average timeframe**: 6 to 9 months for a land title.
blocks.b2_i2: **Registration fees**: 2% to 5% of the market value of the land.
blocks.b2_i3: **Annual Land Tax**: approximately 0.1% of cadastral value.
blocks.b2_i4: **Additional costs**: boundary marking, notary, servicing if land is undeveloped.

procedure_terrain.advice: Important advice: it is strongly recommended to seek assistance from qualified local experts (surveyors, land lawyers) to navigate these procedures.

fiscalite_incitations.title: Taxation and Incentives
fiscalite_incitations.description: Benefit from **incentive tax regimes** and exemptions for your priority investments.
fiscalite_incitations.dialogIntro: Cameroon has implemented an attractive tax policy with significant incentives to attract investment.

blocks.b1_i1: **Pioneer Enterprise**: exemptions of up to 10 years (5 years installation + 5 years operation).
blocks.b1_i2: **Special Economic Zones (SEZ)**: 0% VAT, CIT reductions, administrative facilities.
blocks.b1_i3: **SME Regime**: reduced CIT rate of 25% instead of the standard rate.
blocks.b1_i4: **Export Benefits**: VAT exemptions and customs facilities on inputs.
blocks.b1_i5: **R&D Credits**: tax incentives for companies investing in research.
blocks.b2_i2: **VAT**: standard rate of 19.25%, with exemptions for basic necessities.
blocks.b2_i3: **Customs Duties**: from 5% to 30% depending on product category.

resources.r2: Tax Benefits of the Investment Code (API)

resolution_conflits.title: Dispute Resolution
resolution_conflits.description: Cameroon offers **effective mechanisms** for dispute resolution, including international arbitration.
resolution_conflits.dialogIntro: To ensure a peaceful business environment, Cameroon offers various mechanisms ranging from amicable to international arbitration.

blocks.b1_i1: **Mediation and Conciliation**: mediation chambers (CCIMA) for amicable and confidential solutions.
blocks.b1_i2: **OHADA Arbitration (CCJA)**: awards directly enforceable in all member countries without exequatur.
blocks.b1_i3: **National Courts**: competent for commercial disputes, with modernising procedures.
blocks.b2_i1: **ICSID**: member since 2016, allowing foreign investors to submit disputes to the World Bank.
blocks.b2_i2: **New York Convention (1958)**: ratified, facilitating recognition of foreign arbitral awards.
blocks.b2_i3: **Bilateral Investment Agreements (BIA)**: specific international arbitration clauses in several BIAs.

liberte_entreprise.title: Freedom of Enterprise
liberte_entreprise.description: The country is committed to the **continuous improvement** of the business environment, with simplified incorporation procedures.
liberte_entreprise.dialogIntro: Anyone, national or foreign, is **free to undertake** any lawful activity in Cameroon. Incorporation formalities have been grouped and simplified.

blocks.b1_i1: **One-stop shop**: the Business Creation Formalities Centres (CFCE) handle all the steps.
blocks.b1_i2: A company can be set up in **3 days** once the file is complete.
blocks.b1_i3: The share capital of an SARL is **freely set** by the partners.
blocks.b1_i4: OHADA **entrepreneur** status to start with lighter formalities.
blocks.b2_i1: Freedom of establishment and to carry out any **lawful activity**.
blocks.b2_i2: Some regulated activities require prior **approval** or a licence.
blocks.b2_i3: Equal treatment between national and foreign investors.

rse.title: CSR and Sustainable Development
rse.description: Integrate **Corporate Social Responsibility** and benefit from advantages for a positive impact.
rse.dialogIntro: Cameroon encourages **responsible** investments that respect the environment and benefit local communities.

blocks.b1_i1: Compliance with the **framework law on environmental management** (1996).
blocks.b1_i2: **Environmental and social impact assessment** (ESIA) required for the projects concerned.
blocks.b1_i3: Compliance with the Labour Code and health and safety standards.
blocks.b1_i4: Contribution to the **local development** of host areas.
blocks.b2_i1: Easier access to **green financing** and international partners.
blocks.b2_i2: Benefits for projects that create jobs and respect the environment.
blocks.b2_i3: Better project acceptance and lower risks.

rse.advice: Plan the environmental and social impact assessment from the project design stage: permits often depend on it.

liberte_capitaux.title: Capital Flows
liberte_capitaux.description: **Free movement of capital** is guaranteed, facilitating transfers and repatriation of funds.
liberte_capitaux.dialogIntro: Cameroon guarantees the free movement of capital, a major asset for international investors.

blocks.b1_i1: **Profits and Dividends**: free transfer after payment of local taxes.
blocks.b1_i2: **Royalties and Licences**: patents, trademarks, technologies and technical service payments.

accordions.summaryTitle: How to identify and access land for investment in Cameroon?
accordions.details: To identify and access land for investment in Cameroon, you can consult local land services, real estate agencies, or specialized online platforms. It is also recommended to contact local authorities for information on available land and acquisition procedures.

accordions.summaryTitle: What types of land are available for industrial, commercial, or tourist projects?
accordions.details: The types of land available for industrial, commercial, or tourist projects include industrial land, commercial zones, agricultural land, and tourist zones. Each type of land has specific characteristics and regulations.

accordions.summaryTitle: Is there a national database of available land for investors?
accordions.details: Yes, there is a national database of land available for investors. This database is generally managed by land authorities and can be accessed online or in person at local land offices.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the conditions to obtain a land title or concession in Cameroon?
accordions.details: To obtain a land title or concession in Cameroon, you must follow an administrative procedure that includes submitting an application, verifying documents, assessing the land, and obtaining approval from the competent authorities. Specific conditions may vary depending on the type of land and intended use.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the average timeframes to obtain land for economic use?
accordions.details: Average timeframes to obtain land for economic use can vary depending on the complexity of the file and administrative procedures. Generally, it can take from a few months to a year.

accordions.summaryTitle: How to resolve a land dispute related to an investment project?
accordions.details: To resolve a land dispute related to an investment project, it is recommended to consult a lawyer specialized in land law and follow the legal procedures in force. Local authorities may also offer mediation services to help resolve conflicts.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the steps to register a business in Cameroon?
accordions.details: To register a business in Cameroon, you must follow several steps, including drafting the articles of association, registering with the trade and companies register, obtaining a tax identification number, and registering for social security.

accordions.summaryTitle: What types of companies are recognized by Cameroonian law?
accordions.details: The types of companies recognized by Cameroonian law include limited liability companies (SARL), public limited companies (SA), general partnerships (SNC), and limited partnerships (SCS). Each type of company has specific characteristics and requirements.

accordions.summaryTitle: What formalities must be observed to employ foreign workers?
accordions.details: To employ foreign workers, you must obtain a work permit for each foreign employee. This includes submitting an application to the competent authorities, providing supporting documents, and complying with immigration and labor regulations.

accordions.summaryTitle: How to formalize a partnership with local investors?
accordions.details: To formalize a partnership with local investors, it is recommended to draft a partnership agreement detailing the terms and conditions of the collaboration. This agreement must be signed by all parties involved and may require notarial validation.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the estimated timeframes and costs to set up a company in Cameroon?
accordions.details: The estimated timeframes and costs to set up a company in Cameroon can vary depending on the type of company and administrative procedures. Generally, it can take from a few weeks to a few months, and costs may include registration fees, lawyer fees, and administrative taxes.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the best practices for developing a business project in Cameroon?
accordions.details: The best practices for developing a business project in Cameroon include conducting a market study, developing a solid business plan, finding local partners, complying with local regulations, and engaging with local communities.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the tax advantages for new investments?
accordions.details: Tax advantages for new investments in Cameroon can include tax exemptions, tax reductions, and financial incentives for projects in priority sectors. These benefits are generally defined by the country's tax laws and investment policies.

accordions.summaryTitle: Are there special economic zones (SEZ) or free trade zones in Cameroon?
accordions.details: Yes, there are special economic zones (SEZ) and free trade zones in Cameroon. These zones offer tax and customs incentives to attract investment and foster economic development.

accordions.summaryTitle: What economic activities benefit from specific incentives?
accordions.details: Economic activities that benefit from specific incentives include the agriculture, manufacturing, tourism, information and communication technology, and renewable energy sectors. Incentives can include tax benefits, subsidies, and technical support.

accordions.summaryTitle: Is it possible to benefit from tax or customs exemptions for innovative projects?
accordions.details: Yes, it is possible to benefit from tax or customs exemptions for innovative projects, particularly those that contribute to the country's economic and technological development. These exemptions are generally granted by tax and customs authorities based on specific criteria.

accordions.summaryTitle: How to access support programs for small and medium-sized enterprises?
accordions.details: To access support programs for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), you can contact government agencies, chambers of commerce, and business support organizations. These programs can offer grants, low-interest loans, training, and consulting services.

accordions.summaryTitle: Is equipment imported for projects exempt from customs duties?
accordions.details: Equipment imported for projects may be exempt from customs duties under certain conditions. These exemptions are generally granted for projects in priority sectors or for equipment that is not available locally.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the rights and duties of investors in Cameroon?
accordions.details: The rights and duties of investors in Cameroon include compliance with local laws and regulations, environmental protection, payment of taxes, and contribution to the country's economic and social development. In return, investors have the right to protection of their investments and fair treatment.

accordions.summaryTitle: Are profit transfers abroad guaranteed?
accordions.details: Yes, profit transfers abroad are guaranteed subject to compliance with tax regulations and foreign exchange procedures. Investors can repatriate their profits after payment of applicable taxes and fees.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the protection mechanisms for foreign investors?
accordions.details: Protection mechanisms for foreign investors include bilateral investment treaties, guarantees against expropriation, the right to fair and non-discriminatory treatment, and access to dispute settlement mechanisms.

accordions.summaryTitle: How to manage a commercial or tax dispute as an investor?
accordions.details: To manage a commercial or tax dispute as an investor, it is recommended to consult a specialized lawyer and follow the legal procedures in force. Dispute resolution mechanisms include mediation, arbitration, and competent courts.

accordions.summaryTitle: What international agreements protect investments in Cameroon?
accordions.details: International agreements that protect investments in Cameroon include bilateral investment treaties, tax conventions, and investment protection treaties. These agreements offer guarantees and dispute settlement mechanisms for foreign investors.

accordions.summaryTitle: How are investors supported to secure their projects?
accordions.details: Investors are supported by government agencies, chambers of commerce, and business support organizations to secure their projects. These bodies offer consulting services, information on investment opportunities, and administrative support.

accordions.summaryTitle: What are the current investment opportunities in Cameroon?
accordions.details: Current investment opportunities in Cameroon include the agriculture, energy, infrastructure, information and communication technology, and tourism sectors. These sectors offer growth potential and incentives for investors.

accordions.summaryTitle: Where can statistics and market studies on promising sectors in Cameroon be found?
accordions.details: To find statistics and market studies on promising sectors in Cameroon, you can consult government agencies, chambers of commerce, international organizations, and specialized online platforms. These sources provide data and analysis on market trends and investment opportunities.

accordions.summaryTitle: What services are offered to investors to facilitate their procedures?
accordions.details: Services offered to investors to facilitate their procedures include administrative assistance, legal and tax advice, mediation services, training, and financial support programs. These services are provided by government agencies, chambers of commerce, and business support organizations.
